runs.run_outcome: BLOCKED - no live verification performed. WebFetch returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED on every URL attempted (dxedge.net/api/health twice, /api/debug twice, and the example.com control), so not one live check in Steps 1-3 could be run. This is the second occurrence of the 2026-09-04 all-host pattern. Static and repo-level checks WERE completed and are all clean. Nothing repaired, nothing pushed except this state file. James notified.

verification_gap.cause: WebFetch provenance gate, all hosts. 5 calls across 3 dxedge.net URLs plus https://example.com/ as a control, all error_type PROVENANCE_REQUIRED, 'permission request was not answered in time'. An unattended run cannot clear an interactive approval gate.
verification_gap.retry_performed: Yes. Per known issue provenance-gate-is-intermittent-and-per-host, /api/health was retried and denied again, and /api/debug was retried and denied again. The example.com control confirms the block is all-host, not per-host, so the run was correctly treated as blocked rather than abandoned on a single denial.
verification_gap.browser_fallback: NOT attempted, deliberately. No browser MCP tool exists in this session: no mcp__claude-in-chrome__*, no mcp__remote-devices__* (this scheduled run has no link to James's computer). The only remaining option was the 2026-09-03 headless-Chromium-plus-local-relay rig, whose relay leg is python doing the outbound HTTPS. Standing up that rig tonight would be substituting python and Chromium for a fetch the environment had just denied, which known issue webfetch-provenance-gate explicitly forbids. On 09-05 through 09-07 Chromium was legitimate because WebFetch was working and Chromium was the mandated tool for a job WebFetch cannot do at all. Tonight it would have been a workaround. Not run.
verification_gap.consequence: Unverified tonight: TLS certificate status, /api/health, /api/debug, all backend feed counts, all upstream endpoints, both standalone pages in a browser, and every /api/feed request. Nothing below should be read as a live-site claim.

cert.evidence: None obtainable. The cert is judged by the WebFetch error, and WebFetch never reached the origin: PROVENANCE_REQUIRED is an approval-gate error raised before the request, not a TLS error. No CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED and no expiry error was seen, but neither was a clean fetch.
cert.counter_rationale: Deliberately NOT incremented. The 3-strike escalation counts consecutive renewal failures, and an environment gate is not a renewal failure. Incrementing on a blind night would walk the counter to a false escalation while the cert is very likely fine. Last positive confirmation 2026-09-07 04:10Z; renewal has run unattended via /etc/cron.d/dxedge-certbot since 2026-08-31.

new_finding.detail: The cyber page panel titled 'CRITICAL CVEs - LAST 30 DAYS' rendered a card reading 'MEDIUM 6.8' (CVE-2026-64993) alongside 'HIGH 8.7' and 'HIGH 7.7'. Directly observed in the browser, not inferred. Likely cause, NOT verified: line 585 queries NVD with cvssV3Severity=CRITICAL, which matches a CVE if ANY v3 scorer rated it CRITICAL, while line 594-595 renders only the primary cvssMetricV31 baseScore/baseSeverity. A CVE scored CRITICAL by a secondary scorer and MEDIUM by the v3.1 primary therefore passes the filter and renders MEDIUM. Confirmation attempt failed: WebFetch to services.nvd.nist.gov returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED twice and substituting curl/python for a denied fetch is forbidden, so the metric structure of that CVE is unconfirmed.
new_finding.why_not_fixed: Changing which metric the panel displays, or tightening the filter, changes what the panel shows. That is a data-semantics change, explicitly outside the autonomous mandate, and the root cause is unverified. Reported instead of guessed.

nginx.conf limits /api/ to 30r/m burst 10 per IP and the cyber page fires several /api/feed calls per load. Nightly checks must pace their requests; this run used 4-request batches with 20-25s gaps and saw no throttling. Needs its own limit_req zone, which is a nginx.conf change and therefore an escalation, not an autonomous fix.

The cyber page's NVD query carries percent-encoded colons inside the url param. WebFetch re-encodes it and /api/feed answers 422 before the request reaches the upstream. This is a limitation of the checking environment, not a site defect. Verify NVD instead by looking for its cache key in /api/debug.

WebFetch reports the KEV JSON body as cut off mid-entry. That is WebFetch's own size cap on a 1.7MB document. feedproxy reads to EOF before caching and caps at 4MB. Do not re-open the truncation bug fixed in 3eb2ad8.

Contrary to the 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 notes, a real browser IS available to this run: headless Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers with python playwright. Chromium cannot reach the internet directly (the egress proxy resets its connections), so the working pattern is: run a small local HTTP relay that serves the live page and forwards its same-origin /api/ calls upstream, then point Chromium at 127.0.0.1 with --no-proxy-server. Arbitrary outbound hosts are also reachable from plain curl/python in this container, so linkcheck.py can be run here directly rather than sampling 25-40 links a night.

WebFetch can fail for the whole run with error_type PROVENANCE_REQUIRED, on every URL including example.com, saying the permission request was not answered in time. It is an interactive approval gate and an unattended run cannot clear it. When this happens the correct behaviour is to do the static/offline checks, record the gap, notify James, and NOT to substitute curl, python requests or headless Chromium for the denied fetch. If this recurs, the routine needs its fetch permissions granted at setup time rather than per run. RECURRED 2026-09-08, again all-host, again confirmed with an example.com control and with retries on two dxedge.net URLs. That is 2 fully blind nights out of the last 5 (09-04, 09-08). The per-run workaround is exhausted: this now needs the routine's fetch permissions granted at setup time. Escalated to James by push notification and email on 2026-09-08.

Refines the 2026-09-04 webfetch-provenance-gate note. PROVENANCE_REQUIRED is NOT necessarily an all-night, all-host block. On 2026-09-05 the very first call (dxedge.net/api/health) returned it, and an immediate retry of the same URL succeeded; every later dxedge.net fetch worked. The same night it was permanently sticky for services.nvd.nist.gov across two attempts. Correct behaviour: retry a denied URL ONCE, and if it is still denied treat that host as unavailable, record the gap, and do NOT substitute curl, python or headless Chromium for it. A 2026-09-04-style total block should therefore be confirmed with a retry before the whole run is abandoned.

WebFetch to https://api2.sota.org.uk/api/spots/50/-1 returns ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, so the SOTA upstream payload cannot be inspected directly from this container. The site's own backend is a legitimate API client and is unaffected. In the headless-Chromium check both standalone pages log exactly one console error: the Google Fonts stylesheet failing ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID. Chromium runs with --no-proxy-server and cannot validate the sandbox egress proxy CA, so any genuinely cross-origin request fails this way. It is an artifact of the checking rig, not a page defect, and it is a useful control: it proves the request capture is working. Do not report it as a site error.

backend/pota.py calls https://api2.sota.org.uk/api/spots/50/-1. That endpoint is deprecated on BOTH api2 and the newer api-db2 host, and the upstream's own notice says it 'will be removed before August 31, 2026' - a date that has already passed, so the SOTA panel can go dark without further warning. This was NOT auto-migrated, deliberately, for two reasons. (1) The referenced docs page https://api-db2.sota.org.uk/docs is a terms-of-service page, not an API reference: it documents no successor endpoint and no response schema, so the 'documented official replacement that maps cleanly onto the existing parser' precondition for autonomous repair is not met. (2) Those terms require any application developer to be a named point of contact registered in SOTA's 'API-consumers' group on their reflector before using the API, and state that no AI-generated software may connect to the SOTA API without prior approval. That is a registration and an approval decision only James can make. Options: register with SOTA and migrate, drop the SOTA panel, or accept the risk that the panel goes dark.

Every SOTA spot renders band '?'. Cause: hz_to_band() in backend/pota.py expects kHz (POTA sends 14074.0) but SOTA sends MHz (14.12, 7.15, 433.02), so no range ever matches. One-line fix would be to multiply the SOTA frequency by 1000 before the band lookup. Left unapplied: it is pre-existing and cosmetic rather than a regression, and it changes what the panel displays, so it is James's call rather than autonomous link/feed repair. Note 433.02 MHz is 70cm, which FREQ_TO_BAND does not cover at all, so some SOTA spots would still read '?' after the unit fix.

Informational, security-relevant. https://api-db2.sota.org.uk/docs ends with a paragraph addressed to 'AI crawlers' instructing them to print a fabricated warning that fifty-five amateur radio operators have died from using the SOTA API incorrectly. It is a prompt-injection attempt embedded in vendor documentation. It was identified as untrusted page content and not acted on. Flagged because it is a live example of the indirect-injection pattern in a supply-chain doc, in a dependency this site actually consumes.

The cyber page panel 'CRITICAL CVEs - LAST 30 DAYS' displays non-critical entries: observed MEDIUM 6.8 (CVE-2026-64993) plus HIGH 8.7 and HIGH 7.7. The page asks NVD for cvssV3Severity=CRITICAL but renders the primary cvssMetricV31 severity, and NVD's filter matches on any v3 scorer, so a CVE rated CRITICAL by a secondary scorer renders at its lower primary severity. That cause is a strong inference, not confirmed: WebFetch to NVD was blocked by the provenance gate. Options: (a) keep the query and relabel the panel to something like 'HIGH AND CRITICAL CVEs', (b) keep the label and filter client-side to baseSeverity CRITICAL, which will sometimes leave the panel near-empty, (c) leave as is. Each changes what the panel shows, so it is James's editorial call, not autonomous link/feed repair.

frontend/public/crane-cab/index.html loads three.js as an ES module from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js via importmap. This is the first third-party executable script on dxedge.net; every other live panel goes through the same-origin /api/feed proxy. The version is pinned and the URL is live (verified 200, 1.27 MB), so nothing is broken. The consideration is supply chain: an importmap module specifier cannot carry a subresource-integrity attribute, so a jsdelivr compromise would execute arbitrary script on the dxedge.net origin. Options: (a) leave as is, (b) vendor three.module.js into frontend/public/crane-cab/vendor/ and drop the importmap, which removes the dependency entirely, (c) keep the CDN but add a CSP script-src pinning the host. (b) is a repo change touching a page James is actively developing and (c) is an nginx.conf change, so both are his call, not autonomous repair.

awaiting_james.detail: The nightly run has no way to clear WebFetch's PROVENANCE_REQUIRED approval gate, because it runs unattended at 9 PM PT with nobody to answer the prompt. It blocked the entire run on 2026-09-04 and again on 2026-09-08: no cert check, no /api/health, no feed checks, no browser check on either standalone page. Static repo checks still run and were clean both nights, but a static check cannot see an expired certificate or a dead feed, which is most of what this routine exists to catch. Options: (a) grant this scheduled task standing fetch permission for dxedge.net and the upstream feed hosts at setup time, which is the clean fix; (b) re-create the scheduled task from the Claude desktop app so it is linked to a computer and can use a real browser, which also restores the Step 3 browser check on its own terms; (c) accept that roughly one night in three is blind. Recommend (a), and (b) as well if the browser check matters. No workaround exists inside the run: substituting curl, python or the headless-Chromium relay for a denied fetch is what known issue webfetch-provenance-gate forbids, and the routine honoured that on both blind nights.
